tips.comment: Physique looked an unlucky loser at Doncaster, running too freely and winning the race on the near side of the course at Doncaster, but only 4th behind Dark Thirty. He should get his revenge on three pounds better terms.
Dark Thirty won this last year when 4 lbs heavier than today. He returned from a break last month to a C3 win and will be all the better for that run. He gets my vote while running off an 89.

Elmonjed signed off last season with a bang, landing the valuable Constantine Heritage Handicap at York and looking like there was more to come. The form from his previous win has worked out well too, and he’s clearly progressive. Back from a break but should be spot on and looks a big contender again.

Three-time winner Aramram looks the one to be with here. He won at Nottingham last May and then won handicaps at Doncaster in September and Wolverhampton in October. He started this season with two narrow defeats at Kempton last month and Southwell 10 days ago. He is off the same mark here and, having won on soft, should benefit from forecast rain. He looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Woodhay Wonder has done well over this distance and is also pretty good on this ground too. Has a great chance here.
Ran well in this race last year when 2nd, and this 4-year-old may have more to offer this season. 1 lb lower than when a close 5th in the Sprint Final at Windsor on final start last season.

More Thunder is interesting, the lesser supported of two William Haggas runners. Formerly with Michael Stoute and only had five runs. Acquitted himself fairly well with one win but tried over a longer trip of ten furlongs. Sharply dropped in trip on debut for new trainer. Stoute was famous for bringing his horses along slowly. Dam was a sprinter and Listed winner over six furlongs, so... nine pounds lower than the more fancied stablemate... there might be some potential here off the current rating of 87 over this much shorter trip.
Found switch from AW to turf tricky LTO when 10 of 19 at Doncaster last month, but is also a C&D winner. Now with a dropped mark, I do fancy his chances despite going up in class.

Might be worth an interest on this Quinn runner who has run okay on the all-weather and won't mind the return to turf. In fact, not had the run of the race the last two times, and this one could run into the frame.

Finally ended a shocking losing run when landing a win at Yarmouth last September. But the raised mark and switch to AW proved too tricky for him LTO at Southwell last November, and things will not get easier going up in class. The mark remains unchanged but will welcome a return back to turf.
Sallaal won his only race at Yarmouth last year despite a slow start and the jockey dropping the reins towards the finish. Should show improvement as a three year old and could win here.
On his only debut at Kempton, he won like a 2/5 favorite should. What I liked was the rapid turn of foot that put the race to bed. He should progress from this class, but this is a nice race.
Ran well in a Group 1 in France on his final start last season, despite the form not being the strongest. Ticks all the boxes coming into this, though, and his experience could prove crucial.

Was a big eyecatcher on debut when finishing strongly over a mile on good ground and that maiden at Sandown has thrown up a few winners. The winners include my fancy who won next time out at York showing a good attitude to battle back once headed. The fourth that day Bryant has chased home a couple of very smart horses in Furthur and Kenneth already this season and form could be smart. Looks as if this trip will suit based on his finishing efforts and yard in rare old form with a small sample being five winners from last ten sent out. Looks an ew play to nowt here with trip and ground looking perfect.

Nightwalker was third in a G3 before the break, with the winner that day going on to win again in G3 after the break and taking on weight. My pick has now changed yards, which often puts a bit more spring in the step and could go well in today's comany.

Has impressed in 3 starts and really did the business when winning at Chester last August. It also helps that he has course experience, but improvements are needed, especially because he is going up in class.

Law Of Design was out of his depth in the Royal Lodge on soft ground, racing over 8f for the first time in a hot Group 2, but he’d looked progressive before that and is much better judged on those earlier efforts. The return to a sounder surface looks to be in his favour, and with the yard having won this race last year, he’s a live outsider if back to his best.
Ottoman Fleet won this race last year and will like the firmer going at Newmarket to obtain his first win since June when he won both a Grade 3 and a Grade 2 race at Churchill Downs on firm going.

Ambiente Friendly sets the clear standard on his UK and Irish Derby placings and wasn’t disgraced in the Prix Niel, though his form did dip a bit after those big runs. Down in trip here which should help freshen him up, and while he can be a tricky ride, he’s got the class edge and ought to go very close if anywhere near his best.
Not disgraced on return over a trip that may have stretched her. Should come on for the run and handles quick ground well. Ryan Moore is a positive sign. Big player.
First Conquest may be the second choice for Godolphin here, but this horse has been racing recently over in the Gulf and has got a prime opportunity to run well here with some match fitness.
Verse of Love has bags of potential and has been running well. You would have to think in this company it will be good enough to claim another victory.

Arabian Dusk ran a blinder when third in the Cheveley Park over 6f and brings the standout form into this. She’s versatile with ground and if she returns in similar shape, she’s a big player and sets the bar on reappearance.
An impressive winner on her debut over six furlongs at Haydock, who is entered in the 1000 Guineas at Newmarket. Apparently, done well over the winter and could be anything.

Celestial Orbit improved throughout her two-year-old career, ending it with two wins, including a win in a Listed race at Sandown in her last race, and should be good enough for at least a place here.
Won on final start last season on quick ground and looks a filly on the up. Despite the long absence, she's entered in the 1000 Guineas, which shows the trainer's interest. Good each-way bet.

She showed considerable improvement, successfully making her all-weather debut with a favourable 2f longer distance, displaying her intelligence, she led the race despite starting from a wide position and was never in serious trouble after the final furlong. After a good start, she took charge, ran free and was urged on in the last furlong, finishing strong. She has potential for further progress, but needs to further raise her performance level here, even with a proficient trainer and a skilled jockey. But betting each-way at 28/1 looks like a promising option for a profitable return.

Already a C&D winner in her short career so far and should welcome a return back to turf after an okay effort LTO at Southwell last October. Huge outsider not helped by going up 2 classes but still overpriced for me.

The stable and jockey could have a very profitable day today. This Well Bred filly should hopefully be primed for this and could be very hard to beat. Her dam, 'Chasing Dreams', won this race back in 2019. There's a lot to like about this filly.

Yard 3-5 with their 2yo's this season already and jockey Clifford Lee on Saturday said they've got a nice bunch of juveniles this year. Likely sort on paper and an expensive purchase to boot. Must be followed with yard's 2yo's flying.

Guernsey Lady is bred to be sharp, by top miler Coulsty and a half-sister to a useful 6f performer. Dam was a fair sprinter too, so 5f should be right up her street. Looks like the type to be effective early and worth keeping an eye on, especially if she’s tuned up first time out.
Victory Queen is a half-sister to the very impressive Coroebus for the same connections and this horse has been well found in the market early on. Has a great chance here.

Mahogany Bay was too keen on debut at Newmarket’s July course but should settle better with that run behind him and now steps up in trip, which could suit. The race experience gives him an edge over a few here, and the jockey booking looks a positive switch. Trainer and jockey combo is profitable in turf non-handicaps, so he’s one to keep on side.

Has made light work of his two starts to date on the AW, most recently going off at very short odds, 2/5fav, when beating 'Island Hero' comfortably by 2 and a 1/4 lengths back in January. This well-bred, improving type could be very hard to beat now stepping up in trip if just as effective on turf.

Brindavan didn’t get the ideal setup last time at Kempton with a steady pace but was still only beaten a length and a half off 82. Up in trip now which should suit, and he’s got the benefit of experience over some of these. With a strong jockey booked, he ought to go close.

9/1 with 4 places on offer looks very attractive. Been gelded since winning a valuable and competitive affair over course and distance last October. If anywhere near the form he showed then, which was truly memorable, he must go well under an eye-catching jockey booking.

Only 2/11 winning favorites, however, 8/12 top 3 in the betting. Decent form over 6f and 7f last season, including a comeback G3 win to beat Ramatuelle. Then 0.5L 4th in the French Guineas before Jean Prat flop. Back in business this season with G2 2nd in Meydan over a mile and a listed win back at 6f. Looks now as if she'll be campaigned as a sprinter and being in receipt of weight all around her has the perfect opportunity to make a winning return to home soils.

Fever Dream's only win came in a three-mile hurdle race at Perth on good to firm going, which set his chase mark too high at 109 but has now fallen to 97. He has yet to try three miles over fences, and his jumping has been letting him down in most of his chases so far. But after wind surgery, he could come back refreshed to stay on past Cloudy Wednesday here at Southwell, as that horse has struggled to hold on late off his current mark.

Comes into this with a bit to prove at present, but at least sits on a nice mark with ground conditions in his favor this time. The trip would be a slight worry. He's yet to win over this distance. He has won over slightly further, however, and also placed over CD off a 6lbs higher mark when finishing a close 2nd behind Prince Cleni, which was a solid run given he was lumbered with 12st and gave 20lbs in weight to the winner. He has won at this course in the past, beating Happy Du Mesnil off a 3lbs lower mark than this, beating the runner-up by a narrow margin. That actually rates decent form for this level. Happy Du Mesnil was coming into this race off the back of a win, and I'd still say he was well handicapped off the mark he ran off. The ground is key to his chances. Fast ground is what he needs. If he runs to form here, he'd have a decent chance in this type of race.

The model I run has Dysania to win with Sean Bowen on board, coming in ahead of Fever Dream in second and Cloudy Wednesday in third. Dysania is the oldest horse here, but has got the lowest weight to carry for the 3 mile trip and should be able to make the most of that advantage. RPR is at the higher end of the field, even if OR is slightly low. I would caution that both Fever Dream and Cloudy Wednesday are running with Wind Ops for the first time and may be a bit of an unknown quantity.
A win was had at Uttoxeter last year over today's distance but hasn't gone as close thereafter. Recent third wind operation which may set him up again if not fully perforated.
Stardhem had been running very well and winning, so you would have to give this another chance in this company. Will go well.
Pep Talking won when second up after a break last month by 4L, which makes me think the 5 lbs rise might not be enough to slow him down while keeping Gavin in the saddle.
Stardem should go well, but this Bowen runner is not great over hurdles. However, it might prove a revelation now chasing. It will have been well scored, and there has been some market interest.

King Of The Hill was unplaced in four points and remains a maiden after twelve races under rules but he has finished 2nd in two chases including last time at Warwick after a 285 day break and on his lowly mark of 77 he could go close again.

the model I run has Kientzheim to win for Nicky Henderson with Nico De Boinville on board. The win probability suggests c.31% which translates to around 3.2 so you could argue 2.6 is a low price for the probability. The model suggests next best is Serious Challenge with a win probability of 21% so if you believe the 10% difference is big enough, the price might be worth swallowing. Kientzheim has the highest RPR, the second highest OR and has the joint lowest weight to carry here.

Dropped in class from the Imperial Cup (Class 2) at Sandown to this Class 4. Has 12st but has carried similar weights before. Looking at the Imperial Cup, he was only beaten just over 5l and running on at the finish, which is by far the best form here. Can lead or be handy.
I'll try the same theory as today, where the Skelton yard needs some pot money and sends just Jacksbar here and puts it up in distance. Looks a player.
Probably a better chaser than a hurdler, but he has a smart record when fresh and plenty of winning form here. This quicker surface than he ran on last time he was here will be a big help.
Has won over this course and distance. Came back into form last time out when coming 6th at Newbury 25 days ago and can go well off a falling handicap mark.

The model I run suggests Art of Diplomacy can win this race, coming in ahead of Ballela Blaze in second and My Gift To You in third. This has largely been driven by the highest RPR in the field, the highest OR and previous good finishes at this 3m trip recently.

Rare Clouds makes a stable debut following a 131-day break. Has won and gone well here previously and also won and run close when fresh. 2lb below last winning mark now after a spell in the doldrums following his last win. Capable enough on his day and enough pointers to believe he will be giving it his best shot in this.

The model I run suggests Dublin to Milan will win this one, ahead of Easte Agle in second and Heaven Smart in third. This does look like a tight race, and there is a marginal difference between the expected win probabilities of these horses at the top of the market. Dublin to Milan has a reasonably high RPR and OR compared to the rest of the field, with 6 lbs less to carry than the others ranked higher. My main concern would be that others at the top of the market have completed course and distance before, and this is a step up in trip for Dublin to Milan.
Probably needed the race fourth, beaten 7 1/4 in a handicap hurdle over 2m7f at Bangor-on-Dee latest, but ran well for a long way. Just 2lb above last winning mark; contender.

There's a good run in the locker in the not too distant past for EAST EAGLE. It may only be one run, but he's worth a play at this price. Now 10lbs lighter than the run at Market Rasen in October and gets back to the distance and going of that run here. You can't rule out that the wind op brings about a turnaround and coupled with the preferred conditions, we might get a bounce back here. Underline that might though!
Luminoso sets a decent standard with a runner up finish on debut at Southwell earlier this month. This expensive yearling can win this en route to much richer pickings.

This 6-year-old. Who has raced only once on the flat, finished last in a field of 5 during her debut at Wolverhampton 28 days ago. She is stepping up in distance, and while she needs improvement, her in-form trainer has secured the talented Jack Doughty to help elevate her performance. With a 3lb claim in their favour, their chances look promising. At 66/1, an each-way bet offers excellent value.

Dianarina was tried at Saint-Cloud last year, failing probably due to heavy ground. Returned to the UK, it resulted in a promising runner-up of 12 at Lingfield in this distance and category, two weeks ago. Little She and Be An Angel have claims to make this triumph not easy.

Newfangled has been holding form well and wasn’t beaten far at Lingfield last time over 10f. Drops back to a mile now, which plays to his strengths as a strong finisher, and his consistency makes him a threat in a race like this.

Was impressed with Ciotog's last run, even though slow out of the stalls. Ciotog managed to run from the back and pass most of the field to get 3rd at a big price of 22/1. Last win was at Wolverhampton off a mark of 67, running off 68 here, but Billy Loughnane should be able to get this horse in a better position early on to be able to see daylight for the final furlong.

The 9-year-old achieved 3 wins from 19 starts last year, with his latest victory coming at Chelmsford in March. Unfortunately, he placed 10th out of 21 in a recent handicap at Doncaster 16 days ago, where he was not ideally positioned. Nevertheless, he has a history of winning at this distance, and with a trainer in good form and the talented Dave Egan riding, an each-way bet at 22/1 seems a worthwhile consideration.

Calanthe ran another honest race at Doncaster and continues to hold her form well. She stays a mile strongly, is rarely far away, and looks set to be right on the premises again in a race that should suit her style.

Won twice here back in November at both the mile and the seven-furlong trip from nice low draws. Has been close a couple of other times and comes here on a winnable mark, picking up another nice low draw. The 47-day break shouldn't be a problem here.

This lightly raced horse makes her debut for a new stable here today. Quite simply, he doesn't book Daniel Muscutt without good reason, and I suspect he thinks he may have the horse ready to step up off this mark of 60, having been powered 5lb since her debut handicap run. Clearly, the horse needs to progress, but the stable does really well on the AW (a 16% strike rate). We might now see the true ability of the horse, which has been placed in an AW maiden where the 4th has since won off 70, so she's clearly got the ability to win a race of this nature.

Ectocross hasn’t shown much lately and was well beaten over 12f last time, but he’s back from a break and drops in trip, which could help. There’s been a hint of overnight support and he’s on a workable mark if bouncing back, so not entirely out of it if the break has freshened him up.

Invincible Melody lost ground at the start last time at Wolverhampton but finished well and wasn’t beaten far, suggesting there’s more to come. Trainer’s in form, she’s consistent and still open to improvement, so she’s definitely entitled to be thereabouts again.

Gelded son of Dark Angel who was last seen at Kempton 20 days ago where finishing a nearest finish 5th/10 at odds of 16/1 and shaped better than that bare result suggests as he wasn't ideally placed out wide on the occasion however showed enough promise under the circumstances and was also returning from a 142 day break on the occasion so he is entitled to strip much fitter this time out and with a good draw coming out of gate 3 here at Kempton he is likely to be better positioned this time out and can be a lot sharper at the finish this time out now arriving in a fitter state with a run under his belt currently operating and easing mark of 66 Dr R Newland & J Insole's inmate can begin to trouble the judge especially in what looks to be a suitable looking assignment here jockey Cieren Fallon takes the ride and can give Knights Gold the perfect ride here at Kempton . Respected .

Prince Of Joy hasn’t shown much in maidens so far and was well beaten here last time, so he’ll need to take a big step forward to make an impact off this opening mark. That said, the trainer-jockey combo does well in all-weather handicaps (121 runs, 14 wins, 1.06 A/E, +28pts @ 23% ROI), so he’s not one to completely rule out if finding improvement now handicapping.

Equalised was disappointing at Doncaster but it’s too soon to write him off completely. His maiden run showed he’s got ability, and he’s still learning the game. If he bounces back to that level, he’s more than capable of getting involved in this sort of company.

Still yet to win after 8 starts isn't ideal. However, there has been some promise in several of his runs, including last time out when 2nd at this course and distance, which he also had previously achieved a 2nd in his only other run over C&D. He is 2 lbs higher today for that run last time out, but he is related to 3 6f dirt stakes winners, so he could have the class to see this out.

Significantly dropped back in grade from last year's campaign. Billy Loughnane takes the saddle again, which is a great signal and well drawn to get up early on. 11/1 feels very overpriced and certainly worth a chance.

My Mate Kev got the job done at Chelmsford last time when well backed, and while the form doesn’t look strong, he did show a good attitude to win. He starts handicapping off a fair mark and looks in the mix if stepping forward again.

This 3 year old, a C&D winner in October, finished 7th of 8 in a handicap at Lingfield 22 days ago. Should she manage to return to form, she could be a formidable competitor, especially with Dave Egan riding. The stables track record of 2 wins and 2 places from 4 runs here adds to her appeal, making her a promising each-way option at 33/1.

Is thriving at present and can strike again while in current mood at a track that clearly suits after winning very comfortably over today's course (7f) on the AW in a Class 4 Handicap earlier this month when beating 'Artician' easily by 5 and a 1/2 lengths. It can shrug off a 5lb higher mark with George Wood again on board.

Blue Day had a bit of traffic trouble at Doncaster last time but still ran with credit and was consistent throughout his 3yo campaign. Still unexposed and open to progress, he returns from a break with a minor chance if ready to go.

Intervention ran a cracking race 7 days ago when returning to turf in a Class 2 handicap at Pontefract (5f), finishing 4th of 10 and not beaten far. That was after 8 runs on the all-weather, winning a Class 4 over 7f at Lingfield late March. The step back up a furlong will suit, along with the return to Kempton (4th of 12 last September when here last in a 6f Class 2 off of 84). Mason Paetel takes off a handy 7lb again, bringing his mark to a very attractive 75 and back into calmer waters (Class 4) makes this a very good each-way bet.

Liosa was going the right way on the all-weather last autumn and did well to win at Southwell despite racing keenly. She’s back from a break with a strong jockey booked and if she’s tuned up, she’s got solid each-way claims in a race like this.

Eminency returns after a long break of 241 days, so hopefully, he will be fit to do himself justice. He has had wind surgery, and the trainer has sent out 2 winners from his last 3 runners. Eminency has run here once before and was beaten by less than 2L.

Federated looked smart when bolting up at Newcastle and backed that up with a solid third off 73 last time. The return to a longer trip should suit and with his profile still pointing upward, he’s got a strong chance of going close again.

This was a tough race for me to look through based on Bas Bleu not having a run since October last year. But off her last run at course and a slightly reduced distance, she holds the top average speed on AW of this class. In her last win, she finished in front of Speriamo, who went on to win at Wolverhampton in a class 4. So Bas Bleu has the ability to do better in this class 5. If kept fit at the yard, she should be able to return to Kempton fit enough to take this field on. The value is there, so this is my e/w selection.

Pursuit Of Truth caught the eye last time at Wolverhampton when well backed and not beaten far over 9f. Up in trip now which could suit, gets in here off a light weight, and with a notable jockey booking, he’s a definite contender if finding a bit more.

At the top third of the handicap mark with a 3lb claimer and no wins yet, but has been showing some encouraging signs. This was also evident last time out when a credible 4th of 9 at Chelmsford earlier this month. It has a chance with a dropped mark and dropping down in class.

Detroit Lion is still a maiden after 7 starts, but he has been placed 3 times, finishing runner-up in his last two starts. He was second at Southwell last month and then stepped up to 1m4f at Pontefract last week, again finishing second. He is off the same mark here and looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Second over course and distance back in October, class 4, Damascus Steel has had 3 months rest and dropped in rating and weight. Could be ideal fresh.
I'll try a small each way on Brodies Boy, back on a mark and scene of its only win. Gets Eddie Greaterex up today, who does well for P Atterwater.

Strong Foundations has got in this competitive handicap off a nice low weight and has the assistance of the excellent claimer Freddie Mitchell in the saddle to take off a further 3 lbs. He has got one or two really nice pieces of form and he ran very nicely last time out when stepped up to this sort of trip. He looks well over-priced at 25/1.

Mr Hope Street went into my notebook when seen last on 28th Dec as it was a great effort over an inadequate trip. Still unexposed over a staying distance and with the Skeltons desperate for winners this one looks to have been well placed and can go well.

This is a cracking 3 mile handicap hurdle and Long Draw was a strong fancy for the Pertemps at Cheltenham but didn't quite make the cut, so although he hasn't run since Boxing Day, he is bound to be fit for this, especially given his excellent trainer. Hope Street looks an obvious danger as he was being prepped to run a big race at Aintree but didn't turn up for some reason.
